title: Research: audit native acceptance of odd scatter multiplicities (no new kappa)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This answers PR #3004's open next question 3 for one explicit full-size word, the selected PR #589 word. Appending `[4,4]` to row 0 `[4,5,6,7,8]` triples an existing slot: the complete symbolic checker and both actual native checkers accept it, and all three exporter artifacts equal the selected baseline byte for byte. Both modes of PR #2992's simple-support guard reject it intentionally. Appending `[0,0,0]` instead introduces an absent slot: symbolic and exported actions agree but both fail the defining endpoint. PR #2977's paired-absent `[0,0]` reproduces symbolic acceptance with native rejection.

This is a finite source-bound boundary audit, with a separately written harness and an elementary explanation of the two odd cases. No new parity characterization, supplier admission, physical cost improvement or kappa is claimed. The four synthetic fixtures keep the nine distinct retained helpers and every other word field fixed. Frozen predecessors and the selected result are unchanged.

| Fixture | Occurrences / scatter ADDs | Full symbolic | Native legality | Native columns | Both guard modes |
|---|---:|---|---|---|---|
| selected baseline | 527 / 527 | pass | pass | pass | accept |
| append `[0,0]` | 529 / 528 | pass | pass | reject | reject |
| append `[4,4]` | 529 / 527 | pass | pass | pass | reject |
| append `[0,0,0]` | 530 / 528 | reject | pass | reject | reject |

Native rank mass stays 5129, with nine COPY/ERASE pairs. The accepted triple has the baseline's 27,234 records and 24,305 total ADDs. Both bad streams have 27,235 records and the same 98-column discrepancy at output 111; dirty input column 472 is a one-bit witness. A textual occurrence count is not the emitted ADD count.

The registered primary replay (about 10 s) and all seven behavioral groups pass; the explicit native replay takes about 15 s. Compiles are serial and use the source-pinned checked-128-bit cpp_int stand-in, with a backend-selection probe. This is not a fresh system-Boost build.

Controls: exact one-bit dirty witness; all 64 assignments of a separate six-register scalar fixture; malformed COPY/ERASE lifetimes; every live input corrupted in turn; occupied output preservation; separate check-only and export-only validator bypass mutants; occupied receipt refusal; omitted scatter ADD and truncated native stream. The two native bad-word rejections produce no success receipts.

Publication byte check passed for all 22 package/input files. The exact commit was exported with `scripts/export_research_package.py`, checked, and extracted into a read-only Git-free tree. Optimized native replay (14.729 s) and all seven behavioral groups (2.376 s) passed there; all 23 files including the export manifest remained byte-identical. Full native receipts are retained in `NATIVE.json`; only verified elapsed times and a temporary stream path are normalized. `RESULT.json` retains all scalar discrepancies and exporter hashes.

Not checked: full selected cold ancestry; a new generator/tuner replay; native system-Boost or second-compiler reproduction; physical hosting/projector/bank realization; all-size/compiler, precision/tape and analytic transfer; supplier adoption; hosted CI; independent human or proof-kernel review. Native replay is explicit (`--native`) and is not silently included in the standard-library registered hook.

## Open next questions

The package README and TASK.json retain the actual decision: should a separately versioned successor retain simple supports, or admit multiplicity while binding emitted ADD counts and retained-slot semantics? Start with this four-fixture table and PR #3128's alias premise. Maintainer source-binding/admission review and complete supplier obligations remain blockers. No further local search is justified by this result alone.

## Workflow feedback (optional)
